newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: New listings dominate slow Singapore stock market.
newsitem.headline: New listings dominate slow Singapore stock market.

text.p: New share listings dominated the Singapore stock market on Monday, taking most of the volume and many of the gains, dealers said.

Topping the volume was Wee Poh Holdings, which debuted on Monday more than 70 percent above its initial public offer price of Singapore $0.45. It closed at S$0.835 with more than 53.6 million shares traded.
Other recent listings on the actives board included Nobel Design, Ossia International, F.J. Benjamin and Kian Ann.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed 5.32 points up at 2,193.41. Market volume was 162.2 million shares.
Falling shares led gainers by 193 to 152.
"Take away new listings and there was very little done," said one dealer. "Blue chips were only slightly stronger."
He said the activity in new shares was due to the 100-times over-subscription of Wee Poh's shares at its initial public offer last week and by some spectacular gains by recent share issues.
Among blue chips, Singapore Telecom gained 12 cents to end at S$3.38 after reporting a better than expected 13.6 percent increase in its first-half net profit last week.
